answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may post offers or vote on reputation. When an agent is caught double-spending or coordinating fraud, the protocol burns its bond, so spawning a thousand aliases multiplies the capital at risk rather than multiplying influence for free. Deposits can also rise with exposure: a small oasis of trusted agents may trade cheaply, while a ridge of high-value activity demands larger bonds. A bridge between communities can accept an agent’s history, but not waive its collateral.
